title: Stroop Interference Laboratory
summary: An original colour-word interference task. The learner predicts where the neutral condition will sit, runs practice trials and then a scored block naming ink colours, and reads a summary that splits the usual single Stroop effect into interference above the neutral baseline and facilitation below it. A trial-mix setting turns the proportion-congruency manipulation into something the learner can run rather than be told about, and a transfer challenge asks what four further changes to the task would do to the effect.
learningObjectives: Separate interference from facilitation using a neutral baseline.
Explain what a single incongruent-minus-congruent difference score hides.
Predict how the effect changes when the proportion of incongruent trials changes.
Describe the asymmetry between naming the ink and reading the word.
Explain why a Stroop difference score is not a measure of a person's cognitive control.
interactionTypes: scored block with results withheld until the end
trial-mix manipulation the learner can run
bar chart paired with a data table
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; reaction times and answers stay in the browser tab as JavaScript variables and disappear on reload, and nothing is written to storage.
accessibilityNotes: The task requires discriminating ink colours, which is the phenomenon rather than a design accident and cannot be removed. Three routes are provided instead: a two-colour set (blue and yellow, which differ in brightness as well as hue), a stimulus panel with one fixed near-black background in both the light and dark site palettes so every ink sits at 7:1 contrast or better, and a worked example that reaches every conclusion on the page without responding to a single colour. Away from the stimulus itself nothing depends on colour: every response button prints its colour name in words alongside its swatch, the chart bars print their own values and the incongruent bar is hatched as well as differently filled, and all results are given as numbers in a table. One word is on screen at a time and it stays until the learner answers - no trial is timed out, nothing fades, moves or animates, and no CSS animation or transition is used, so there is nothing for a reduced-motion setting to switch off. Responses can be given by pointer or by the number keys printed on the buttons; response targets are 3.25rem tall. The stimulus panel is aria-hidden during a run because any useful description of it would state the answer. Every control has an accessible name, headings do not skip, focus moves to the results heading, and forced-colours rules are supplied for the panel, the swatches and the chart. Usable at 320px and at projector widths with no horizontal page scroll; the wide results table scrolls inside its own container.
readmeTopic: Stroop interference: what a neutral baseline adds, and what a difference score is not
simulationNotes: The learner's own trials are real responses, not simulated. Stimuli are original: colour words printed in their own colour (congruent), in a different colour from the set (incongruent), or common non-colour nouns printed in one of the inks (neutral). Neutral items are matched to the colour words only approximately in length, and not at all in frequency or orthographic neighbourhood; the teaching notes say so. Inks are rotated rather than sampled within each condition, so ink identity carries no information about condition. A block is 24, 36 or 60 trials, split a third each way in the balanced mix and one sixth, one sixth, two thirds in the mostly-incongruent mix. Correct responses between 200 ms and 3000 ms enter the condition means; errors, anticipations and lapses are counted and reported separately rather than averaged in. The worked example is simulated with mulberry32 and Box-Muller: RT = base + condition offset + Normal(0, 70) + Exponential(mean 60), floored at 260 ms. Block A is a balanced mix, seed 20260923, 80 trials per condition, base 620, offsets -22 / 0 / +78, accuracy .98 / .97 / .93, and produces interference +78 ms and facilitation +24 ms. Block B is a mostly-incongruent mix, seed 20260987, 30 / 30 / 120 trials, base 640, offsets -6 / 0 / +38, accuracy .97 / .97 / .95, and produces interference +35 ms and facilitation +3 ms. Both seeds were chosen so the sample means land near the generator's parameters; the page says so and treats it as a teaching point about sampling rather than hiding it. The smaller effect in Block B is built into the generator to illustrate proportion congruency, not discovered by it. These numbers are illustrative: they are not norms, not published effect sizes and not anybody's data, and browser display and input timing are uncontrolled.
